When Auto-MDIX handles pinout automatically versus when it is disabled
Cat5e versus Cat6 cabling and RJ-45 termination standards (T568A/T568B)

weeks_data.topic: Router and switch basic configuration; password and SSH authentication; IOS management and recovery

Monday.question: Which device hardening step do you think matters most on a Cisco router?
options: Enable secret password
Console and VTY passwords
SSH instead of Telnet
Backing up the IOS image and configuration

Tuesday.question: Between running-config (RAM) and startup-config (NVRAM), which mistake is most painful to make during a lab?
options: Reloading the device before running copy running-config startup-config
Locking yourself out and saving the broken config to NVRAM
Forgetting no shutdown on a newly configured router interface
Overwriting startup-config instead of backing it up to TFTP

Wednesday.question: When configuring SSH on a Cisco router or switch, which prerequisite step is easiest to forget?
options: Setting a hostname and ip domain-name before generating RSA keys
Configuring a local username and secret password
Setting login local and transport input ssh on the VTY lines
Generating an RSA key modulus of at least 1024 or 2048 bits

Thursday.question: Why is enable secret preferred over enable password and service password-encryption on Cisco IOS?
options: enable secret uses strong hashing while type 7 passwords are trivially reversible
service password-encryption only obscures plaintext passwords from shoulder surfing
enable secret overrides enable password when both are configured
Auditors flag type 7 Vigenere-encoded strings immediately

Friday.question: During a Cisco router password recovery or IOS image recovery in ROMMON, which step requires the most care?
options: Sending the break sequence during the first 60 seconds of boot
Setting configuration register 0x2142 to bypass startup-config
Copying startup-config to running-config after booting instead of overwriting it
Resetting config-register back to 0x2102 before saving

weeks_data.topic: VLAN fundamentals and 802.1Q trunking; Spanning Tree Protocol (STP, RSTP, PVST+)

Monday.question: Which VLAN or Spanning Tree concept do you expect to cause the most trouble in practice?
options: Access ports versus trunk ports
Native VLAN mismatches
Choosing the root bridge
Port states and convergence time

Tuesday.question: When configuring 802.1Q trunking between two switches, why is changing the default native VLAN away from VLAN 1 recommended?
options: Mitigates VLAN hopping and double-tagging attacks
Prevents untagged control traffic from mixing with default user ports
Eliminates CDP native VLAN mismatch warnings when standardized
Forces explicit planning of which VLANs are allowed on the trunk

Wednesday.question: In Spanning Tree Protocol (802.1D / PVST+), how does a switch determine which device becomes the root bridge if priorities are left at default?
options: Lowest MAC address wins when all bridge priorities are tied at 32768
Oldest switch in the closet often has the lowest MAC and becomes root unintentionally
Setting spanning-tree vlan X root primary lowers priority deterministically
Extended system ID adds the VLAN number to the base priority

Thursday.question: When tracing STP port roles across a redundant switch topology, which distinction takes the most practice to spot quickly?
options: Root port (one per non-root switch, lowest root path cost)
Designated port (one per segment, forwarding traffic onto that link)
Alternate/Blocked port (preventing Layer 2 bridging loops)
How link speed changes default STP port cost (19 for 100M, 4 for 1G)

Friday.question: Which STP enhancement provides the biggest practical improvement on access switches connected to end hosts?
options: PortFast transitioning edge ports immediately to Forwarding
BPDU Guard shutting down a PortFast port if a switch is plugged in
Rapid PVST+ (802.1w) cutting convergence from 30-50 seconds to sub-second
Per-VLAN load balancing with different root bridges per VLAN

weeks_data.topic: EtherChannel (PAgP and LACP); GRE tunnels; IPsec and SSL VPNs

Monday.question: Which technology do you expect to use most often in real networks?
options: EtherChannel (PAgP or LACP)
GRE tunnel
IPsec VPN
SSL VPN

Tuesday.question: When bundling physical switch ports into an EtherChannel, which configuration mismatch will prevent the port-channel from forming?
options: Incompatible channel-group modes (for example LACP passive on both sides)
Speed or duplex mismatch across member interfaces
Trunk encapsulation or allowed VLAN mismatch on member ports
Mixing Cisco-proprietary PAgP on one end with IEEE 802.3ad LACP on the other

Wednesday.question: What is the primary reason network engineers pair a GRE tunnel with IPsec (GRE over IPsec) instead of using either one alone?
options: GRE encapsulates multicast routing protocols (OSPF/EIGRP) while IPsec encrypts the payload
Pure GRE provides zero confidentiality or integrity on its own
Traditional tunnel-mode IPsec crypto maps do not carry multicast hellos natively
GRE adds a 24-byte header that requires careful MTU and TCP MSS adjustment

Thursday.question: In a site-to-site IPsec VPN using IKE, which Phase 1 versus Phase 2 parameter mismatch is hardest to diagnose from logs?
options: IKE Phase 1 ISAKMP policy mismatch (encryption, hash, DH group, lifetime, or PSK)
IKE Phase 2 IPsec transform-set mismatch between peers
Non-mirror-image crypto ACLs defining interesting traffic
NAT exemption missing before traffic hits the outbound crypto map

Friday.question: When comparing site-to-site IPsec VPNs with client-based SSL/TLS VPNs, which use-case boundary is clearest?
options: IPsec connects fixed branch offices transparently at Layer 3
SSL/TLS VPNs support remote users over any HTTPS-capable network
Full-tunnel versus split-tunnel routing decisions for remote clients
Certificate-based authentication versus pre-shared keys and MFA

weeks_data.topic: WAN serial links (HDLC and PPP); PPP authentication (PAP and CHAP) and multilink

Monday.question: Which WAN encapsulation do you think is more practical for a link between two different vendors?
options: HDLC
PPP
Frame Relay
Not sure yet

Tuesday.question: On a back-to-back lab serial link (DCE to DTE), why does the link stay up/down or down/down before encapsulation is even checked?
options: DCE side is missing the clock rate command
Encapsulation mismatch (HDLC on one router, PPP on the other)
Serial cable DCE and DTE ends swapped between routers
Interface still administratively shut down

Wednesday.question: Why is CHAP strongly preferred over PAP for authenticating a PPP serial link?
options: CHAP uses a 3-way MD5 challenge-response so the plaintext secret never crosses the wire
PAP transmits the username and password in cleartext during link establishment
CHAP can re-challenge periodically during an active session
Both still require matching hostnames and shared secrets on each router

Thursday.question: When troubleshooting a failed PPP CHAP authentication using debug ppp authentication, which error do you check for first?
options: Username not configured to match the remote router's hostname
Mismatched shared secret password between the two routers
ppp authentication chap missing on one or both serial interfaces
LCP state stuck before reaching the authentication phase

Friday.question: What does Multilink PPP (MLP) provide when bonding two or more serial T1 links between routers?
options: Packet fragmentation and load balancing across member serial links
Single logical Multilink interface for IP addressing and routing
Continued connectivity at reduced bandwidth if one physical serial line fails
Lower serialization delay for small voice or real-time packets

weeks_data.topic: IP routing fundamentals and static routing; routing algorithms; EIGRP

Monday.question: Which routing approach do you find easiest to troubleshoot so far?
options: Static routes
EIGRP
Routing protocols in general
Not sure yet

Tuesday.question: When a router has both a /26 static route (AD 1) and a /24 EIGRP route (AD 90) matching a destination IP, how does it choose the forwarding path?
options: Longest prefix match (/26) always wins before administrative distance is compared
Administrative distance is only used when prefix lengths are identical
Metric is only compared among routes from the same routing protocol and prefix length
Default route 0.0.0.0/0 is used only as a last resort when no longer prefix matches

Wednesday.question: When configuring a floating static backup route on a Cisco router, what makes it stay out of the routing table until the primary dynamic route fails?
options: Setting an administrative distance higher than the primary protocol (for example AD 100 vs EIGRP 90)
Specifying both exit interface and next-hop IP (fully specified static route)
Verifying fallback behavior by shutting down the primary link
Removing auto-summary so classless masks are preserved

Thursday.question: When comparing distance-vector, link-state, and EIGRP's DUAL algorithm, what makes EIGRP converge so quickly?
options: Maintaining a Feasible Successor in the topology table that satisfies the Feasibility Condition (RD < FD)
Sending partial, bounded updates only when a link state or metric changes
Using Hello keepalives to detect neighbor loss rapidly
Querying neighbors with DUAL only when no Feasible Successor exists

Friday.question: When two EIGRP routers are directly connected and ping works, what is the most common reason they fail to form an EIGRP neighbor adjacency?
options: Mismatched Autonomous System (AS) number in router eigrp
Mismatched K-values (metric weights) between the two routers
Used a subnet mask instead of a wildcard mask in the network statement
Interface marked passive-interface under router eigrp

Every router in the OSPF domain must use the same reference bandwidth for consistent SPF calculation

Full SPF recalculation (Type 1 and Type 2 LSAs) stays contained within each area

ASBRs inject external routes (Type 5 LSAs) from redistribution or default-information originate

options: Each user authenticates with individual credentials instead of a single shared password
Revoking one departing employee's access does not require rekeying every device on the WLAN

Friday.question: In a large campus network, why do organizations deploy lightweight APs with a Wireless LAN Controller (WLC) using CAPWAP instead of standalone autonomous APs?

weeks_data.topic: IPv6 fundamentals and static routing; IPv6 EIGRP dynamic routing

Monday.question: Which IPv6 feature do you find most different from IPv4?
options: 128-bit addresses
No broadcast traffic
Stateless autoconfiguration
Link-local addresses

Tuesday.question: When shortening a 128-bit IPv6 address in hexadecimal notation, which rule prevents ambiguity?
options: Double colon (::) can replace a contiguous block of all-zero hextets only once per address
Leading zeros within any 16-bit hextet can always be omitted
Trailing zeros within a hextet cannot be dropped

Wednesday.question: How does IPv6 Neighbor Discovery Protocol (NDP) replace IPv4 ARP and router discovery without using broadcasts?
options: Neighbor Solicitation and Neighbor Advertisement ICMPv6 messages over solicited-node multicast
Router Solicitation and Router Advertisement (RA) messages for SLAAC prefix discovery
Duplicate Address Detection (DAD) before assigning a unicast address to an interface
Every IPv6-enabled interface automatically generates an fe80::/10 link-local address

Thursday.question: When configuring IPv6 static routing on a Cisco router, what happens if you forget the global command ipv6 unicast-routing?
options: Interfaces accept IPv6 addresses and respond to ping, but the router will not forward IPv6 packets between subnets
Link-local next-hop static routes require specifying both the outgoing interface and the fe80:: address
Global unicast next-hop static routes can resolve recursively
show ipv6 route displays connected (C) and local (L /128) entries

Friday.question: When configuring EIGRP for IPv6, which requirement trips up engineers who are used to IPv4 EIGRP?

weeks_data.topic: BGP fundamentals and configuration; BGP advanced topics and route manipulation

Monday.question: Which BGP topic do you expect to find hardest?
options: Autonomous systems and peering
Path attributes
Route filtering and manipulation
Route selection order

Tuesday.question: Why does the global Internet use BGP (a path-vector EGP) between Autonomous Systems instead of an IGP like OSPF or EIGRP?
options: BGP enforces business policy and administrative control rather than shortest link metric
BGP scales to hundreds of thousands of prefixes without flooding link-state databases globally

eBGP (AD 20) and iBGP (AD 200) separate inter-domain from intra-domain routing

Wednesday.question: When a BGP session is stuck in Idle or Active state instead of reaching Established, what is the first thing you verify?
options: TCP port 179 reachability and matching neighbor IP addresses on both routers
Correct remote-as number in the neighbor statement

Thursday.question: In the BGP best-path selection algorithm, how do Weight, LOCAL_PREF, AS_PATH, and MED differ in direction and scope?
options: Weight (Cisco-local) and LOCAL_PREF (AS-wide) influence outbound traffic leaving your AS
AS_PATH prepending and MED influence inbound traffic entering your AS from neighbors
Weight is checked before LOCAL_PREF, which is checked before shortest AS_PATH
Next-hop reachability in the IGP is required before any BGP path is considered valid

Friday.question: Which BGP operational task do you want the most practice with before finishing the course?
options: BGP path selection order
Route filtering with prefix lists
LOCAL_PREF and MED tuning
BGP neighbor states
